design_decision_computed_on_read.sign_off: Computed-on-read SUM is acceptable for this project's current scale. The instance_attachments table has two indexes — (instance_id DESC created_at) and (content_hash) — neither covers byte_size. A per-upload SUM requires a full column scan of the tenant schema. At current scale (1 GiB allowance / 25 MiB per-file ceiling ≈ ~40 max-size attachments per tenant) this is a trivial sequential scan of a small table. Drift-free correctness outweighs the marginal per-upload cost, and the design's argument that delete/2 requires no change is sound.
design_decision_computed_on_read.oq2_index_deferral: ACCEPTABLE. The design correctly notes that a btree index on byte_size does not help a SUM unless Postgres can use an index-only scan (visibility-map dependent). Deferring this to 'if needed in future' is the right call at current scale. No blocking concern.

cross_module_coupling_oq1.sign_off: Letflow.Repository.Attachments aliasing Letflow.Identity.Tenant for Repo.get is consistent with an established codebase-wide pattern. 17 other modules across different contexts (service_catalog.ex, exam/certificate.ex, tenant_onboarding.ex, plugs/tenant_status.ex, platform/migration_rollout.ex, public_read.ex, multiple routers) alias Letflow.Identity.Tenant directly. lib/letflow/repository/attachment_links.ex already aliases Letflow.Identity from the same context. No documented module boundary rule in docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md prohibits this. The tenants table is reasonably treated as a shared global record across the codebase.
cross_module_coupling_oq1.note: The absence of a prefix arg on Repo.get(Tenant, tenant_id) is correct — tenants lives in the global schema. The prefix param in check_storage_quota/3 is only forwarded to get_storage_usage/1 for the per-tenant schema SUM.

notes: alter table(:tenants) inside change/0 with add :storage_allowance_bytes, :bigint, null: false, default: 1_073_741_824 is idiomatic and rollback-safe. Postgres applies the column default to all existing rows at add time; Ecto's auto-reversal in the down direction is remove, which drops the column cleanly.

storage_allowance_bytes is :integer in the Ecto schema (Tenant.ex) but :bigint in the migration. Ecto maps both to Elixir integer, so no runtime issue, but the schema field type and migration column type are inconsistent in declared intent. Filed as an observation; does not block PASS — mismatch is cosmetic (no overflow risk: allowance values are sub-2^53 and well within :integer range).
